diagnoses.description:
The task specification explicitly allows “more than one P (or S) picks or no P (or S) pick per file.” Forcing exactly one P and one S pick per file can inflate false positives on low-SNR or genuinely phase-absent traces, potentially reducing precision and F1.
Evidence: The agent “wrote /root/results.csv (200 rows = exactly one P and one S per file)” and Turn 31 confirms min=max=2 picks per file.
Trajectory location: turn 29 (methodology reflected in final output)

A fixed post-P exclusion window can mis-handle cases with short S–P times, mis-picked P, or emergent onsets; it may force S to a later unrelated peak, harming timing accuracy within the 0.1 s tolerance and lowering recall/precision.
Evidence: The S pick was selected as “argmax of PhaseNet_S constrained to occur at least 0.2 s after the picked P.”
Trajectory location: turn 29 (S-pick constraint logic)

Although time conversion attempts to correct alignment, using a global argmax over the entire probability trace (instead of trigger/peak picking around onsets) is more sensitive to spurious peaks and may reduce pick timing robustness versus standard trigger-based picking, affecting the required 0.1 s accuracy.
Evidence: Earlier, the agent observed a systematic offset between annotate argmax indices and classify-derived pick indices due to annotation trimming/shift, then proceeded using annotate probability argmax with time conversion back to waveform indices.
Trajectory location: turns 20–22 and turn 29 (use of PhaseNet.annotate argmax rather than trigger-based picks)

The run cannot establish that the produced picks meet the required F1 thresholds (>=0.7 for P, >=0.6 for S); structural correctness of the CSV does not imply performance success.
Evidence: The trace shows validation of file/row counts (Turn 31) but no evaluation of pick quality (no F1, no tolerance-based check, no spot-check against any provided labels/weights beyond existence).
Trajectory location: overall (no quantitative validation against ground truth)
